newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-U.S. BANKS BUY MAJOR SHARE IN ITALIAN CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-U.S. BANKS BUY MAJOR SHARE IN ITALIAN CLUB.

text.p: Two U.S. banks joined forces with three Italian businessmen to buy Serie B soccer team Torino Calcio on Wednesday with the hope of restoring the club to its former glory.

The two banks, Merrill Lynch and Bankers Trust, have taken a one-third stake in a company named Bullfin which in turn has acquired an 89.93 percent interest in the club from its current chairman Gian Marco Calleri for slightly more than 20 billion lire ($11.9 million).

The balance of Bullfin is owned by a company called HLS based in Genoa and owned by three businessmen -- Massimo Vidulich, who is to take over from Calleri as Torino chairman, Davide Palazzetti and Renato Bodi.

Palazzetti will be the club's managing director and Bodi, son of Luigi Bodi, who played for the club in the 1950s, will join the board of directors. Neither of the U.S. banks will be directly represented on the Torino board.
Vidulich told a news conference he planned to beef up the team by acquiring new players, win promotion to Serie A and float the club on the London stock exchange before the year 2000.
Torino were Italy's top club in the 1940s, winning the league championship four years in succession. But in 1949 their entire team died in a plane crash in the hills outside Turin.
They have won the league title only once since then, in 1976, and were relegated to Serie B at the end of last season.
Vidulich said he and his partners intended to expand the business by developing merchandising interests and generating sales from pay-per-view television.
